names.official: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

summary: The United Kingdom now requires an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA, £16, valid 2 years) from all visa-exempt visitors — including US, EU and Commonwealth citizens — while visa nationals apply online for a Standard Visitor visa (£127, stays up to 6 months); only Irish citizens are exempt under the Common Travel Area.

defaultStayWindow.text: The allowance runs per visit rather than across a window: the Home Office prices its long-term Standard Visitor visas at “6 months per visit”, and the guide states you can usually stay up to 6 months. There is no published rolling limit on how much of the year those visits may add up to, though a pattern of back-to-back visits is grounds for refusal at the border. GOV.UK does not say whether the days of arrival and departure are counted, so we count both.

source.name: GOV.UK — Standard Visitor: apply for a Standard Visitor visa

fee.notes: Apply via the official UK ETA app or GOV.UK. Every traveler needs their own ETA, including babies and children.
Apply online, then give biometrics at a visa application center. Long-term 2, 5 and 10-year visitor visas are available at higher fees; each visit is still capped at 6 months.
Plus the Immigration Health Surcharge (£776 per year for students). Requires a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from a licensed sponsor. Confirm the current fee on GOV.UK before applying.

source.name: GOV.UK — Skilled Worker visa (fees vary by visa length and role — check the current fee on GOV.UK)

fee.notes: For passing through UK border control between flights, up to 48 hours. A Direct Airside Transit Visa (£35) covers airside-only transit. Fees change periodically. Confirm on GOV.UK.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for the whole of your stay in the UK. No extra validity beyond your departure date is required.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not required for entry, but strongly recommended. The NHS charges overseas visitors for most hospital treatment.

onwardTicket.text: Not a formal requirement, but Border Force officers may ask visitors about return or onward travel plans and accommodation.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is set, but visitors must be able to show they can support themselves (and any dependants) for the whole trip — in the visa application or if asked at the border.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of £10,000 or more must be declared when entering or leaving Great Britain (separate rules apply for Northern Ireland).

source.name: GOV.UK — Taking cash in and out of Great Britain

notes: Personal allowance arriving in Great Britain: 200 cigarettes, 4 liters of spirits (or 18 liters of still wine plus 42 liters of beer), and other goods up to £390.
Bringing meat or dairy products into Great Britain is prohibited from most countries, including the EU.

payments.text: Contactless cards and phone payments are accepted almost universally, including on London buses and the Tube; many cafés and attractions are now card-only.

safety.text: The UK is very safe for visitors. The main petty risks are pickpocketing and phone-snatching in busy central London areas — standard urban precautions apply.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — United Kingdom Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: Late spring to early fall (May–September) brings the mildest weather and longest daylight; pack for rain at any time of year.

idp.text: United Kingdom is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 (UNTS vol. 125, p. 3); Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: United Kingdom is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for United Kingdom yet.

tips.text: Apply for the ETA only through the official "UK ETA" app or GOV.UK (£16) — unofficial websites charge unnecessary mark-ups.
Every traveler needs their own ETA, including babies and children; it is valid 2 years (or until your passport expires) for unlimited visits.
EU, EEA and Swiss national ID cards are no longer accepted at the UK border. All visitors except Irish citizens need a passport.
The NHS charges overseas visitors for hospital treatment. Take out travel insurance with medical coverage before you go.

faq.question: What is the UK ETA and who needs it?
faq.answer: The Electronic Travel Authorisation is a digital entry permission required by every visa-exempt visitor to the UK, including US, Canadian, Australian, Japanese and EU citizens. It costs £16, is valid for 2 years (or until your passport expires) and covers unlimited visits of up to 6 months each. Only Irish citizens and UK visa holders are exempt.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for the UK?
faq.answer: No visa, but they do need an ETA: US passport holders must obtain the £16 Electronic Travel Authorisation before traveling and can then visit for up to 6 months per trip.

faq.question: How much does a UK Standard Visitor visa cost?
faq.answer: The Standard Visitor visa costs £127 for a 6-month visa. Long-term 2, 5 and 10-year multiple-entry versions cost more, and every visit is capped at 6 months. Most applications are decided within about 3 weeks.

faq.question: Can EU citizens enter the UK with a national ID card?
faq.answer: No. EU, EEA and Swiss visitors must carry a passport and obtain a £16 ETA before travel. Irish citizens are the exception — the Common Travel Area lets them enter without either.

faq.question: How long can visitors stay in the UK?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt visitors with an ETA, and Standard Visitor visa holders, can each stay up to 6 months per visit. Visitors cannot work for a UK employer, and frequent back-to-back visits may be questioned at the border.
